title: POC scoping — TTFT vs TPOT sampling & SLA alignment (Starlane Health)
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 2-week POC to validate TTFT (time-to-first-token) and TPOT (total per-output-token) SLOs for Starlane's conversational triage service. Discussed traffic profile, sample sizes for p95/p99 estimates, measurement approach (synthetic vs shadow), acceptable SLO bands, canary plan and required artifacts (benchmark harness, test inputs, security questionnaire). Agreed next steps: Redwood to deliver benchmark harness + draft measurement plan; Starlane to provide representative prompt set, token length histogram, and test credentials for private pilot infra check.
topics: define initial TTFT and TPOT SLO targets (p95/p99)
sampling strategy and statistical significance for p95/p99
workload sizing: concurrency, seq len distribution, batching
measurement plan: synthetic load vs shadow traffic
next_steps: Redwood: deliver benchmark harness repo + runbook (Priya) by 2026-02-18
Starlane: share 2 weeks of token-length histogram + representative prompt set by 2026-02-16
Schedule 30-min follow-up to review initial benchmark results week of 2026-02-23
Exchange security questionnaire and SOC2 summary (Liam) by 2026-02-15
action_items: Priya Kapoor - create and share baseline harness (k6 + custom generator) and example scripts - due 2026-02-18
Marco Ruiz - provide token length histogram and QPS baseline from prod logs - due 2026-02-16
Samir Patel - open firewall rules and provide test VPC endpoint (if Private pilot) - due 2026-02-20
Liam O'Neill - send security one-pager and SOC2 pointer - due 2026-02-15
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11 14:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Neill (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (CTO, Starlane), Erin Cho (ML Eng), Samir Patel (Platform), Dana McBride (Product)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy): scope POC to measure TTFT and TPOT, agree on p95/p99 targets, run bench harness, share datasets and security docs.

00:00 Liam: okay uh good afternoon everyone thanks for joining on short notice, i'm liam from redwood inference, this is priya our se, and we're excited to scope the pilot with starlane, can everyone do quick intros?
00:12 Marco: yeah hi i'm marco ruiz cto at starlane, we own the triage service, focusing on latency for front door chat, appreciate you folks.
00:18 Erin: erin cho ml eng, i manage the inference pipelines and prompts.
00:22 Samir: samir platform, infra and networking.
00:25 Priya: thanks, quick agenda: align acceptance SLOs for TTFT vs TPOT, confirm traffic profile and sampling, define the benchmark plan and timeline, and outline security needs.

00:40 Liam: awesome, to ground the convo — can you describe current pain? what are the real thresholds you care about, like p95 first token or end-to-end cost constraints?
00:49 Marco: sure, our triage chat needs feel near instant for first token, today on our self-hosted setup we see p95 first token ~280ms, p99 closer to 520ms under peak, cost is also important but latency drives product stickiness, if we go above 300ms p95 we see drop in completion.
01:08 Erin: also note avg seq length is skewed — many short prompts ~10-20 tokens but some long context up to 1.2k tokens, and we do a lot of persistent session caching.
01:20 Priya: okay that's helpful — caching reuse will change effective TPOT because prefix kv cache may avoid reprocessing tokens, so we need to capture both cold and warm cache cases in the bench.

01:35 Liam: quick defs so we're aligned: we use TTFT for time-to-first-token, TPOT for per-output-token latency (total time divided by output tokens), we'll propose p95/p99 targets and you can push back.
01:46 Marco: mm-hmm fine.

02:00 Priya: proposed initial SLOs (draft): TTFT p95 <= 250ms, TTFT p99 <= 450ms. TPOT p95 <= 25ms per token, TPOT p99 <= 50ms per token. These are starting numbers — we can tune by model size and qntz profiles.
02:18 Erin: those sound ambitious compared to our current p95 but desirable. How did you get those?
02:23 Priya: empirical across similar workloads on our dedicated pools; depends on model variant, batch sizes, and kernel/quantizashun path. For long sequences p99 TPOT will obviously increase.

02:40 Marco: okay, can we separate cold-start vs warmed-cache? our users are sensitive to first-interaction lag.
02:46 Liam: yes we should. We'll report cold TTFT (empty kv) and warm TTFT (after prefix reuse). Bench will show both distributions.

03:05 Samir: what's your suggested sampling strategy for p99? we worry p99 needs a lot of samples to be stable, and our traffic has diurnal spikes.
03:14 Priya: good point — for p99 you typically need thousands of samples to estimate stably. Our plan: 30-minute steady-state runs at multiple QPS points, with at least 10k requests per run, and repeated runs (3 replicates) to build confidence. We'll also run a long tail sweep to capture spikes.
03:34 Erin: 10k per run might be heavy, will that distort caching patterns?
03:38 Priya: we emulate production patterns: request sequences with session affinity and pre-warmed prefixes for warm runs. For cold runs we clear caches periodically. The harness supports session stickiness.

03:55 Liam: measurement modes — synthetic load vs shadow traffic — thoughts?
03:59 Marco: we prefer shadow for realism but it's trickier to setup. Synthetic is easier to control.
04:05 Priya: recommend both. Start with synthetic to baseline and isolate variables (batch sizes, concurrency, kernel choices). Then run a short shadow run to validate metrics against real traffic. Shadow will surface routing and network variance.

04:25 Samir: regarding deployment — are we testing on Redwood Dedicated or Private? we have constraints about PHI and need to validate KMS integration.
04:34 Liam: Redwood suggested Private for data residency but Dedicated is viable if you can accept outbound logs. We'll include security checklist. Priya can run the bench on a dedicated pool first, then we can mirror to your private infra.

04:50 Erin: for bench inputs we'll share a prompt set, but also we have templated user messages and slot filling — can the harness replay templated variations?
04:58 Priya: yes the harness supports parameterized templates and variable token length distributions. If you share a CSV of user segments we'll map QPS accordingly.

05:18 Liam: let's talk about cannery/canary rollout and acceptance criteria when pilot finishes. What's success?
05:23 Marco: success is hitting p95 TTFT <= 300ms and TPOT p95 <= 35ms on our representative traffic, plus no regressions on quality. If we see p99 breaches we want a plan — either fallback to smaller model or trigger reduced concurrency.
05:38 Priya: we can define automated fallback policies: route to lower-cost model variant or reduce batch sizes on breach, and we can instrument alarms for p99 spikes.

06:00 Erin: on quality regressions how do you measure — do you run eval prompts and check string similarity?
06:06 Priya: we usually tie a small eval set of prompts to quality monitors (ROUGE/BLEU or tokenizer-aware similarity plus human spot checks). We won't change model family without evaluating outputs.

06:20 Samir: network variance — our app is multi-region, do you recommend region-local testing?
06:25 Priya: yes, test in the target region(s) to capture egress and cross-region latency. For the POC pick your highest-volume region first.

06:40 Liam: okay let's nail down the exact benchmarks we'll run during the 2-week pilot. Priya?
06:44 Priya: plan: Week 1: baseline synthetic runs across three load points (low/med/high QPS) for cold and warm cache, 3 replicates each, 10k requests per run. Week 2: shadow run for 48 hours at production QPS sample and a long-tail stress test (12-hour sweep) to capture p99 under burst. We'll deliver a results dashboard with p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, batching stats, and cost per 1k tokens.
07:10 Marco: dashboard format? can you share a sample?
07:12 Liam: yes we'll share an example Google Sheet and a short report template — link in follow-up.
07:18 Erin: curious about batching config — are you adjusting batch size dynamically?
07:22 Priya: runtime can do continuous batching tuned by sequence length profiles; we can pin max batch size for control. For TPOT estimates we run with several batch policies to show tradeoffs.

07:38 Samir: for p99 estimation, you mentioned number of samples — if we can't run 10k due to cost, what's the minimum?
07:45 Priya: minimum is ~3k samples per condition to get a rough p99, but the confidence interval will be wide. We can also use robust tail estimators to reduce sample needs but prefer more samples when possible.

08:00 Liam: any compliance blockers? Marco?
08:04 Marco: we need SOC2 evidence and KMS/HSM integration notes. PHI handling rules require encrypted-at-rest and in-transit, and audit logs. We'll want to see RBAC and SSO setup.
08:16 Priya: we'll attach our SOC2 summary and KMS integration docs; the private deployment supports bringing your own KMS/HSM and provides audit logs via console. We'll note specific RBAC roles in the runbook.

08:32 Erin: how do you measure cost per token in the bench? do you include infra overhead?
08:36 Priya: yes cost breakdown shows GPU runtime, infra overhead, and per-token unit cost based on measured throughput and token counts; we'll include token-level cost and projected monthly cost at your QPS.

08:50 Marco: about model variants — we use an open model family now, can you run quantized versions?
08:55 Priya: yes we support quantized variants; we'll include 8-bit and 4-bit profiles and show performance delta. Note quantization may slightly affect quality; we'll pair that with eval set metrics.

09:10 Liam: let's capture the acceptance SLOs you want to lock into pilot sign-off. Marco, you suggested p95 TTFT <= 300ms earlier — are we locking that as target?
09:20 Marco: yes as an initial acceptance band — if Redwood achieves p95 <= 300ms and TPOT p95 <= 35ms on representative traffic and no quality regressions, we consider pilot successful. p99 should be improved vs our current baseline (current p99 ~520ms).
09:34 Priya: we'll report both absolute and relative improvements. Also include stability over a 48-hour shadow.

09:50 Samir: what's the expected instrumentation? traces, token timings?
09:54 Priya: we emit per-request traces with TTFT and per-token deltas (where permitted), aggregated histograms, and jitter metrics. We can redact content for PHI-sensitive fields.

10:08 Erin: about the harness, what's the language and how easy to run locally?
10:12 Priya: harness is k6 + python generator, containerized, and we can run it from your VPC or our test pool. We provide a runbook and example docker-compose.

10:26 Liam: timeline recap: we'll share harness by 2/18, you share histograms by 2/16, firewall tests by 2/20, and follow-up 2/23 to review initial numbers. Does that look right?
10:37 Marco: yep that works.

10:44 Dana: one quick product ask — if we hit p99 regressions, we want an automatic fallthrough to a reduced-latency mode (shorter context). Can that be configured?
10:52 Priya: yes policy-based fallbacks can reduce context window or model size; we'll show config examples.

11:05 Liam: any other blockers or open questions?
11:08 Erin: just about data residency once more — we'll need a Private deployment check if the Dedicated pool can't satisfy compliance.
11:14 Liam: noted, we'll include a short matrix showing which features differ between Dedicated and Private.

11:24 Marco: thanks all, this was useful. look forward to the harness.
11:28 Liam: great — we'll follow up with links and the runbook. thanks everyone.

Post-call notes (auto): references shared: benchmark harness repo (placeholder): https://github.com/redwood/bbench-harness (priv link will be shared), sample dashboard template (Google Sheet), SOC2 summary PDF.

Potential pitfalls noted in transcript: transcription has minor name misrecognitions (e.g., cannery/canary, quantizashun), speaker labels may shift in auto-caption.

End of transcript.
